In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the three different methods considered here can provide a good estimate of the PBL top in the growing phase of the boundary layer, when the PBL is well defined, but they are less effective during the decaying phase, when the PRL is less well defined.
all the three approaches are able to provide estimates of the boundary-layer height with a satisfactory degree of accuracy.

the use of the rotational Raman lidars for the PBL characterization represents a valid and reliable alternative to the more traditional approaches based on the analysis of the elastic backscatter signals, especially in those cases in which the latter approach is not applicable.

the use of Raman lidar measurements for the determination of the PBL vertical structure and height is an effective tool for studying atmospheric processes.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the PBL height can be determined by means of the first-order derivatives of both the elastic and the rotational Raman lidars signals.
the use of the first-order derivatives of the range-critical Raman lidar signal can be a powerful tool for the estimation of the PBL structure, also in the presence of a residual layer.
